old_caption:
The video depicts a scene set in a modern server room, characterized by rows of tall, glass-enclosed server racks illuminated by green and blue lights. The environment is clean and well-lit, with a high-tech ambiance. Two individuals, a man and a woman, are seen walking through the server room. The man, dressed in a white shirt and black pants, has gray hair and wears a lanyard around his neck. The woman, also in a white shirt and black pants, carries a tablet and appears to be explaining something to the man as they walk. They pause briefly, pointing at one of the servers, indicating a discussion about its operation or maintenance.

As they continue their walk, another individual, partially visible, is seen working on a server in the background. This person is also wearing a white shirt and black pants, consistent with the professional attire of the others. The camera follows the two main figures, maintaining a steady pace as they move deeper into the server room.

caption: The video depicts a narrow aisle inside a server room, flanked by glass-fronted racks glowing in cool blue and dotted with small green status lights that blink independently of the people. A man in a white dress shirt, dark trousers and an ID lanyard moves steadily toward the viewpoint down the corridor, walking beside a woman in similar attire who cradles a tablet and keeps her gaze fixed downward on its screen. Their size on screen stays roughly constant as the corridor recedes, showing the camera tracks backward at a matching pace. Glossy panels on either side mirror the two figures and the racks, the reflected silhouettes shifting in step with the real subjects. Behind the man, a third dark-haired figure is largely hidden, only a sliver showing. As the excerpt progresses, her head and a white sleeve emerge between the two walkers. The tablet woman keeps her head bowed for most of the run. Later she lifts it, turning her gaze toward the man. His own head shifts from a downward glance to a level look.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
